description: Manually curated STRIDE ground truth for the Simple Web API architecture. Each threat is keyed by its target (component_id or data_flow_id) plus STRIDE category; that (target, category) pair is the intended matching key for evaluation. The api_to_db flow is intentionally well-secured (TLS, authenticated, encrypted) and therefore has no ground-truth threats, so it can surface false positives.

threats.description: The public API is internet-exposed and can be targeted by attackers impersonating legitimate clients or bypassing authentication.
threats.mitigation: Enforce strong authentication (e.g. OAuth2/OIDC) and validate credentials on every request.

threats.description: Being internet-exposed, the API can receive manipulated or malicious requests (e.g. parameter tampering, injection payloads).
threats.mitigation: Validate and sanitize all inputs, use parameterized queries, and apply strict schema validation.

threats.description: Without sufficient audit logging, clients can deny having performed actions against the public API.
threats.mitigation: Log authenticated requests with tamper-evident, timestamped audit trails.

threats.description: As a public internet-facing endpoint, the API is exposed to volumetric or application-layer denial-of-service attacks.
threats.mitigation: Apply rate limiting, request throttling, timeouts, and upstream DDoS protection.

threats.description: Flaws in authorization logic could let an authenticated client access resources or operations beyond its privileges.
threats.mitigation: Enforce least-privilege authorization checks on every endpoint and separate roles/scopes.

threats.description: The customer database stores sensitive data that could be exposed through misconfiguration, backups, or compromised credentials.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt data at rest, restrict network and account access, and manage secrets securely.

threats.description: Sensitive customer records could be modified without authorization if database access controls are weak.
threats.mitigation: Enforce least-privilege database accounts and integrity constraints; monitor write access.

threats.description: Without database audit logging, changes to sensitive data cannot be reliably attributed to an actor.
threats.mitigation: Enable database audit logging for access to and modification of sensitive tables.
